How to read this dashboard

Explore the original notebook charts below. Each visualization is paired with an interpretation to help translate the analysis into operational questions and potential actions.

Data integrity note: This HTML uses the chart renders already saved in your notebook, rather than recalculating or fabricating chart data. The chart canvas/background remains the notebook's original styling; the dashboard layout and surrounding interface use a dark theme. Some chart cells may be based on different eligibility filters, so compare rates only when their definitions match.
NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 4

Monthly Appointment Volume (2022–2024)

INTERPRETATION

Appointment volume fluctuates month to month. Use the quarterly chart alongside this view to distinguish seasonal variation from sustained growth.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 5

Quarterly Appointment Volume (2022–2024)

INTERPRETATION

Quarterly totals make broader changes easier to compare; investigate unusually high or low quarters before attributing causes.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 7

Distribution of Appointment Outcomes

INTERPRETATION

The status mix shows how appointments are distributed across outcomes. Prioritize no-shows separately from cancellations because the operational causes may differ.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 10

Booking Channel Outcomes

INTERPRETATION

This chart compares booking-channel share by volume. High-volume channels are important levers for reminders and confirmation workflows.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 13

No-Show Analysis 1. Which specialties and cities have the highest and lowest no-show rates?

INTERPRETATION

City-level no-show rates identify locations that may benefit from targeted confirmation and follow-up. Compare rates together with eligible appointment counts.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 14

No-Show Analysis 1. Which specialties and cities have the highest and lowest no-show rates?

INTERPRETATION

Specialty-level no-show rates help target operational improvements. Interpret rates alongside appointment volumes to avoid overreacting to small groups.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 18

Effect of Booking Lead Time on No-Show Probability

INTERPRETATION

Longer lead times can create more opportunity for plans to change. Consider reminder timing closer to the appointment date for higher-risk lead-time groups.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 21

No-Show Rate by Time of Day

INTERPRETATION

Compare time of day, weekday/weekend, and lead-time patterns. These are associations in the observed data, not proof that the factors cause no-shows.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 24

No-Show Rate by Appointment_Type

INTERPRETATION

Appointment type and booking channel can have different no-show profiles. Tailor interventions to the higher-risk categories rather than applying one message to everyone.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 27

No-Show Rate by Reminder Type

INTERPRETATION

Compare each reminder group with the no-reminder baseline. This is observational analysis, so differences should not automatically be treated as causal impact.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 29

Prior No-Show History vs Future No-Show Rate

INTERPRETATION

Prior attendance history can help identify patients who may need additional engagement. Use it to offer support, not to restrict access to care.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 31

No-Show Rate by Repeat Visit Status

INTERPRETATION

Membership and repeat-visit segments may show different attendance patterns. Compare both rate and sample size before designing segment-specific campaigns.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 33

No-Show Rate by Age Group

INTERPRETATION

Age, gender, and recorded chronic-condition status provide segmentation views. Treat demographic differences carefully and avoid interpreting them as causal.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 35

Visit Reasons Associated with Higher No-Show Rates

INTERPRETATION

Visit-reason rates can help identify appointment types for more tailored engagement. Give more weight to categories with adequate appointment counts.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 37

Age Group Distribution Across All Specialties

INTERPRETATION

This chart compares age-group appointment volume across specialties; it describes demand mix, not no-show likelihood.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 39

Estimated Revenue Lost Due to No-Shows

INTERPRETATION

Potential revenue loss is estimated using average realized revenue for completed appointments multiplied by no-shows. It is an estimate, not booked or guaranteed revenue.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 42

Average Revenue by Specialty

INTERPRETATION

Average realized revenue varies by specialty. Use this for service-mix context, and remember that averages can hide differences in volume and case mix.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 43

Average Revenue by Appointment Type

INTERPRETATION

Average realized revenue by appointment type helps compare service categories; consider it together with appointment volume before drawing business conclusions.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 46

Total Revenue by City

INTERPRETATION

City revenue rankings show where realized revenue is concentrated. Revenue totals are influenced by both appointment volume and average revenue.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 48

Payment Mode Distribution

INTERPRETATION

Payment-mode counts show the observed payment mix. Use this to guide payment experience improvements, not as a measure of patient preference without further context.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 51

Insurance Coverage vs Out-of-Pocket Payment

INTERPRETATION

Average out-of-pocket payment is lower for insured patients in the saved analysis. Coverage terms and patient mix may also influence this difference.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 56

Appointment Volume by Specialty

INTERPRETATION

Appointment volume is highest in the leading specialties shown. High demand can inform staffing and capacity planning, but does not alone measure utilization efficiency.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 59

Average Waiting Time by Specialty and Time of Day

INTERPRETATION

Waiting time varies by specialty and time of day. Review higher-wait combinations for scheduling or capacity adjustments.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 62

Consultation Duration vs Patient Satisfaction

INTERPRETATION

The scatter/regression view explores association between consultation duration and satisfaction. Correlation does not establish that longer consultations cause higher satisfaction.

NOTEBOOK CHART · CELL 65

Dotor Experience vs Consultation Fee

INTERPRETATION

The relationship between experience and consultation fee is exploratory. Fee differences may also reflect specialty, credentials, location, and other factors.
